newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals start week listlessly.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals start week listlessly.

text.p: Precious metals prices were slightly lower in slow, aimless trade on Monday which was expected to continue as the year-end approaches, dealers said.
"With Christmas and New Year's just around the corner, people aren't doing anything," one dealer said. "A $368-$370 range is probably as far as gold is going to go."
Bullion fixed at $368.60 an ounce, compared to $369.00 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $369.30/$369.80.
Prices had drifted slightly lower overnight as brokers squared their books ahead of the holidays and under pressure from a stronger dollar, dealers said.
But Friday's European Union pact on post-monetary union budget stability was having no apparent impact on the gold price so far, dealers said.
"There's been no effect at all, although that may change when New York opens. London seems like it's shut up shop," a dealer said.
The prospect of European Monetary Union (EMU) has cast a bearish pall over the gold market in recent months amid uncertainty over gold's future role in European central banks.

Dealers are concerned that central banks may sell off some of their gold reserves in the rush to comply with EMU criteria. Some analysts said the stability pact would re-fuel optimism about the single currency project proceeding on schedule.
But rumours of sales by a central bank have already accompanied gold's sharp decline to three-year lows in recent weeks, analysts noted.
"The bad news is pretty well discounted," said analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
"Whether (central banks) sell now or in two years, the market has already sold the rumour. This is cold coffee in a way."
The other precious metals were quiet and marginally lower, in tandem with gold.
Silver was down one cent at $4.81/$4.83, and seen trading in a tight trading range between $4.79 and $4.85 in the near term.
Platinum was also $1.05 lower at $367.50/$368.50, while palladium was barely changed at $117.50/$118.50.
Both metals were also seen stuck in a narrow price bank for the time being.
